knowledge_point.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 14.5\cdot 13\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{38}^{∘} \\  & =94.25\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{38}^{∘} \\  & =58.026… \\  & ≈58{\text{ mi}}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of  $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =58-41 \\  & =17{\text{ mi}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
